item.title: Diablo 5 Is Starting With the Worst-Case Scenario the Series Spent Decades Avoiding
item.description:
There were a lot of big announcements at BlizzCon 2026, but one of the most exciting of all was definitely Diablo 5 . Predecessor Diablo 4 has now been around for three years at this point, and even though Diablo 5 is still a few years out from its debut, knowing what comes next after this current chapter is intriguing. Blizzard made sure to keep the game's finer details under wraps, but the developer revealed a surprising amount about the next Diablo entry. Between the release window and story details, Diablo fans have had a lot to celebrate since the announcement.

When it comes to the inhabitants of Sanctuary, though, there is no room for celebration. After decades of players trying to fight off the forces of the Burning Hells, the Lord of Terror has finally taken over the human realm. This is one of the most eyebrow-raising Diablo 5 story details that Blizzard has unveiled, because it teases one of the franchise's darkest narratives yet. All hope is now seemingly gone, and players will have to face the even tougher challenge of having to save Sanctuary from its fate.

New Steam Action RPG Like Diablo Meets Vampire Survivors Is Incredibly Addictive

This new Steam action RPG blends Diablo-style progression with Vampire Survivors-like combat, and it’s dangerously hard to put down.

By Josh Cotts

Diablo 5 Brings the Apocalypse to Sanctuary, Marking the Dark End of a Franchise Era

Traditionally, players have always been fighting to push back the apocalypse in the Diablo games. Fighting against evil to save humanity is a classic storytelling trope, and Blizzard is flipping the franchise's staple premise on its head. Blizzard simply revealing a Diablo 5 announcement would have been intriguing enough, but revealing this key piece of the main story is a wild way to generate hype, especially so early in the game's development.

Even though the official Diablo 5 release date hasn't actually been revealed yet, Blizzard confirmed at BlizzCon that the next entry is expected to arrive in Spring 2029 at the earliest. That leaves a lot of time for fans to speculate about what the game has to offer, so Blizzard getting ahead of the rumor mill and confirming certain details is understandable. It builds anticipation and sets a few main expectations, but it also leaves plenty of unanswered questions about what went wrong to make Sanctuary's fall possible in the first place.

Three classes have been confirmed for Diablo 5 , two returning and one new. The returning classes are the Demon Hunter and the Monk, while the newcomer is called the Plague Knight.

Diablo 5's Story Is Set Decades After the Events of Diablo 4

Diablo 5 takes place a whopping 100 years after Diablo 4 , which leaves the latter in a tough narrative spot. Blizzard confirmed that there won't be any major new Diablo 4 expansions between now and Diablo 5 . For a lore shake-up as significant as Sanctuary succumbing to the Lord of Terror's rule, one or two new DLCs would have been solid ways to bridge the gap between Diablo 4 and Diablo 5 's stories to help paint a clearer picture of how the human realm's defeat was possible.

No more new expansions for Diablo 4 definitely wasn't the news that players were wanting to hear, but the bright side is that Blizzard's seasonal support isn't slowing down any time soon. The game will still get regular seasonal updates that can serve as a replacement for expanding the lore. These updates may not be as significant as full-blown DLCs, but each update could plant further breadcrumbs that set in motion the events that will eventually cause Sanctuary to crumble under the Lord of Terror's power. Most updates will probably be centered around features like the new Diablo 4 Amazon class, but there is at least time between entries to expand the overarching story in increments.

In Diablo 5, Sanctuary Has Forced Humans Into a Nomadic Life Centered Around Survival

Another key difference in Diablo 5 's gameplay is that players are resigned to a life on the road. Conquering strongholds and finding safety in town hubs are no longer part of the equation. Nowhere is safe, so players and their parties have to keep moving to make sure that everyone lives another day. Building a caravan of allies will play an integral part in Diablo 5 , and that allows Blizzard to showcase Sanctuary in an all-new way. From vendors to loyal companions, each NPC that players meet along the way could become an important resource.

Two Diablo 5 caravan companions have already been confirmed by Blizzard. One is a former Sister of the Sightless Eye and the other is a Treasure Goblin who has lost their purpose, since this broken version of Sanctuary has rendered greed meaningless.

Diablo 5 's caravan system is inspired by campsites in games like Baldur's Gate 3 and Dragon Age , and it could be the added change of pace that makes the next chapter extra compelling. Of course, it's too early to say for sure if Diablo 5 's caravan system nails its premise, but it's definitely an intriguing tweak to the usual formula.

Now that Blizzard has unveiled a few fascinating bits of information about the next Diablo game, only time will tell when fans are given more news to keep them satisfied until 2029. Details like Diablo 5 taking inspiration from Diablo 2 and revealing three classes are setting some high expectations that are going to be harder to meet as the years pass. Revealing these kinds of details so early on could either work in Blizzard's favor or leave too much time for fans to build up assumptions that the game is unable to fully deliver on.

Everything Officially Confirmed About Diablo 5
Diablo Immortal's Blood Knight Sends a Clear Message for Any Future Diablo 4 Classes
Why Dropping Microtransactions Gives RuneScape a Shot at World of Warcraft's Crown

Either way, the Diablo 5 news has been fun to dive into. On top of the Diablo 5 announcement, Blizzard has even confirmed that a Diablo Netflix show is currently in development. The past week has been big for Diablo lovers, which has left a lot of information to unpack. Blizzard hopefully reveals more information at next year's BlizzCon, but that remains to be seen. In the meantime, there is still plenty of time to enjoy Diablo 4 and theorize about the events that will eventually lead to Sanctuary's fall.

item.title: Nintendo Issues New Official Statement About Zelda: Ocarina of Time and the Switch 2
item.description:
Nintendo has spent much of 2026 celebrating some major milestones for tentpole games like Pokemon and The Legend of Zelda , which celebrate their 30th and 40th anniversaries this year, respectively, as well as the 1st anniversary of the Nintendo Switch 2. And the Nintendo of America president discusses its plans, specifically around the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and Nintendo Switch 2, at the Technology Summit.

Of course, The Legend of Zelda is especially positioned for a super busy period, with Nintendo preparing both new game-related releases and other projects connected to the franchise. At the very least, fans know they are getting the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake in November and the live-action Zelda movie early next year.

Brand-New Switch 2 Console Bundle Revealed

A new Nintendo Switch 2 console bundle arriving in the coming months will offer some digital goodies to customers in a specific region.

By James Ratcliff

Nintendo of America President Discusses Ocarina of Time Remake, Switch 2

Nintendo of America president and COO Devon Pritchard briefly discussed the company's plans for The Legend of Zelda and Switch 2 during an interview with Variety at the aforementioned summit. Pritchard pointed to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, which is coming exclusively to the Switch 2 in November, as one of the major pieces of what Nintendo has planned. In her own words, "This is just the beginning." Pritchard also made clear that Nintendo has a lot of plans for the Switch 2 beyond these anniversaries as well. According to Pritchard,

"We’re at the beginning of Nintendo Switch 2...We’ve already had some really wonderful experiences, both ours and third-party, come to the table, and I can’t wait to see what the system is going to do and what our talented developers will bring to the table."

Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.

Round 1

Which one doesn't belong?

0 / 10
10.0 s

Results

0/5

Best: 0/5

—

More Games

Nintendo has already seen both its own games and third-party releases make an impact on the system during its first year, with truly exclusive Nintendo Switch 2 games outpacing both PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, but the gaming department is only one thing on the president's mind. She was keen to highlight Nintendo's partnerships with companies such as Sony and Sony Pictures (for the Legend of Zelda live-action movie) as part of a broader effort to bring its experiences to existing fans while also reaching new audiences.

For Nintendo, the longer-term strategy goes beyond simply releasing more games for its biggest franchises, even if its IPs do get revisited faster than many other companies. Pritchard said the company is focused on creating experiences that can build relationships with audiences across generations, even as consumers have more entertainment options than ever. That's how Nintendo video games avoid losing players to TikTok or other time-consuming distractions. The Switch 2's first year and Zelda 's 40th anniversary only represent the opening stretch of a much larger period for Nintendo's major IP.

Nintendo Issues New Official Statement About Zelda: Ocarina of Time and the Switch 2
Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Is Making One of the N64's Biggest Limitations Impossible to Hide
Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Map Officially Reveals Major Change
The Witcher 3 Remastered and Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Seem to Have Their Labels Backward

Of course, fans will just have to wait and see how the Nintendo Switch 2 shakes out. Its sales are up, the console is beloved, and a game like Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is the console-seller it needs right now (as well as Pokemon Winds and Waves in 2027). 10 years from now, if not 20, 30, or 40, it'll be interesting to look back at the Nintendo Switch 2 generation, and it seems Nintendo wants those memories to keep players around for decades.

item.title: How to Equip Held Items in Aniimo
item.description:
Held Items are important equipment for your Aniimo, since they can enhance their power, defense, and abilities. You might have obtained some here and there, but the question is: How can you equip them? The problem with Held Items is like most of the content in Aniimo, is that it's locked behind certain prerequisites. Learn how to unlock Held Items, how to obtain more, and how to equip them on your Aniimo with this guide.

Which Free Prismana To Choose in Aniimo

Which free Prismana to choose in Aniimo? First Starter Choice Explained and Prismana Aniimo Guide.

By Lucas Simons

How To Unlock & Equip Held Items in Aniimo

Held Items can be obtained by defeating Alpha Aniimo or by finding them after completing Sanctuaries, Special Events, or Journey Discoveries. They vary in shape, effects, and qualities (Blue, Purple, Gold), but they share one thing in common: They cannot be equipped right away. This happens because you must be at least Student Level III to unlock the Held Item Slots on your Aniimo.

So, first, you need to complete a series of quests that include various parts of the Elite Training Core Courses, leveling up your character, and then answering a questionnaire (Dr. Lewis at the Outpost). Once you have reached Student Level III, you can finally equip Held Items.

Now, let's talk about Qualities:

  • Blue Quality (Rare) Held Items are often disposable or used to fuel Enhancement on Purple Held Items.
  • Purple Quality (Epic) Held Items are extremely good, but not the top of the charts. These will be the ones you will be using mostly throughout the adventure.
  • Gold Quality (Legendary) Held Items are the ones you want to have once you've reached the end game. They are often obtained by completing Companion Handbook (Season Pass) Levels, or certain Aniimo Events.

To Equip Held Items, you need to open your Aniimo Management Tab (P) , then select the Aniimo you want . Then, select the Training Menu (bottom right). After that, select the Held Item Tab (top right).

You might notice these Held Items have various effects and levels . This means they can be enhanced. Next, we will discuss how to upgrade Held Items in Aniimo .

How To Upgrade Held Items in Aniimo

To upgrade Held Items in Aniimo , you can sacrifice other Held Items of Lower or the Same Quality, or use Held Item Cores, which are obtained from Chests, completing Elite Training Objectives, or defeating Alpha Aniimo.

Take into consideration that using Held Items of the same value to upgrade another will increase the number of upgrade levels you get, though in terms of economy, it is less efficient than using Cores.

Each time you upgrade a Held Item, its core stats increase, making its effects more powerful and consequently increasing the power of the Aniimo that has it equipped.

item.title: How to Get a Ray Gun in COD Warzone (Ghost Train Mystery Box Easter Egg)
item.description:
The Haunting update for Call of Duty: Warzone has arrived with Black Ops 7 Season 6, and while players may be grinding to get a new secret free Camo, there is another Easter Egg that players can complete. By stopping the Ghost Train on Haunted Hollow, you can open the Mystery Box and, if you are lucky, get the legendary Ray Gun Wonder Weapon. Here is how to get the Ray Gun in Call of Duty: Warzone .

Endgame Forbidden Summoning Event Guide (Black Ops 7 Aether Worm Bossfight)

Completing the Forbidden Summoning World Event in Black Ops 7 Endgame gives players a bunch of rewards. Here is how to beat the Aether Worm fast.

By Nathan Round

Step #1: Stop the Ghost Train Using the Signal Lever

How to Stop the Ghost Train on Haunted Hollow in Warzone

Before you can get the Ray Gun, you must first stop the Ghost Train on Haunted Hollow. To do this, head to any of the following POIs and look for a signal lever:

  • Train Station
  • In between Main Street and the Riverboat
  • Lumbermill
  • Coal Depot

Once you see the Ghost Train approaching your location, turn the lever to signal the train to stop. You must do this with plenty of time to spare before the train reaches the signal light, otherwise it will keep going. Successfully stopping the Ghost Train will make it shift back to a regular train, allowing you to climb aboard.

Step #2: Spin the Mystery Box to Get the Ray Gun

How to Get the Ray Gun on Haunted Hollow in Warzone

Now that the Ghost Train is stopped, the Mystery Box will appear on one of the rear carriages. From here, you can spin the box for a random Legendary Weapon. If you spin it long enough, you will also have a chance to get the Ray Gun Wonder Weapon from Zombies.

However, do note that you only have a limited number of spins before the train becomes a Ghost Train again, after which it will move to another location. You can repeat the previous step again to increase your chances of getting the Ray Gun.

If you are successful in getting the Ray Gun, you can use it for the rest of the game unless you drop it yourself or are eliminated by another player. The Ray Gun has an ammo reserve of 100 rounds by default , and you can actually resupply this ammunition.

The Ray Gun also deals splash damage just like it does in Zombies , though you will notice that its fire rate is fairly slow, since many players often use it with the Double Tap Perk inside of the co-op Zombies mode.

The Ray Gun also deals splash damage just like it does in Zombies , though you will notice that its fire rate is fairly slow, since many players often use it with the Double Tap Perk inside of the co-op Zombies mode.

item.title: New Metroidvania on Steam Is a Breath of Fresh Air After Hollow Knight: Silksong
item.description:
I'll say up front that I enjoy a good challenge when it comes to video games. I can get down with soulslikes, challenging metroidvanias, and action RPGs that make me think twice about my character's build. However, there are plenty of times I just want to play a game that has the mechanics and tone of those genres without feeling like I need to tip-toe my way through an environment because I'm not sure when something is going to delete me in one hit. Thankfully, there are games like that out there, and Kyle Thompson's upcoming metroidvania Well Dweller is proof. In fact, after spending nearly an hour with its demo on Steam , I want so much more of it, as its emphasis on traversal puzzles over combat, its unique Tim Burton-esque art style, and its cozy atmosphere and lighthearted tone are what I didn't realize I was craving after fighting my way through Hollow Knight: Silksong .

I need to go ahead and note that Well Dweller isn't only coming to Steam on September 22, 2026, either, as it will also be launching on Xbox Series X|S, PS5, Nintendo Switch, and Nintendo Switch 2. So, if you're as into playing metroidvanias on a handheld console as I am, and you don't own a Steam Deck but do own either Switch, you're in luck. But apart from its platforms, I simply can't emphasize enough how much of a breath of fresh air this is if you're looking for a metroidvania that, according to its demo, is a little on the lighter side. That being said, Well Dweller can still be challenging if you don't keep your wits about you, and its boss fights, especially, still require you to think. It's also possible that things ramp up in the full game after what I played in the demo, but based on my experience alone, it already feels like one of the best metroidvanias to play if you want a change of pace for once.

10 Near-Perfect Metroidvanias That Nobody Remembers Today

They may be less popular, and most gamers may have forgotten about them, but these Metroidvanias still rip.

By Tristan Jurkovich

Well Dweller Is Charming, Cozy, and Cool

Check Out Well Dweller on Steam

Before I dig into Well Dweller 's combat, let me get into what this game is really trying to sell—again, based on my limited time with its demo. Yes, there is combat, and it's fun, but the heart of this experience is its world, its atmosphere, and its traversal . Actually, the majority of Well Dweller 's demo revolves around solving traversal puzzles and, in standard metroidvania fashion, backtrack-heavy exploration. And when I wasn't exploring or fighting off weird-looking monsters, I was charmed by the characters and the presentation, both visual and audible.

Wishlist Today

Glimmer, Well Dweller 's protagonist, is a tiny bird armed with little more than a matchstick, and he basically gets thrown into the role of unlikely hero when his family is torn apart. His siblings have been snatched away from their home, leaving Glimmer to venture out into this strange, rotting kingdom to find them and eventually make his way to the wicked Queen responsible for so much of its misery. His ultimate goal is pretty straightforward: reunite with his siblings, save his family, and burn the Queen. It's a surprisingly dark setup for a game that can be so downright adorable at times, especially once you start meeting Glimmer's siblings and seeing how they interact with one another. But I think that's a huge part of what makes Well Dweller such a unique metroidvania. The world around these characters is grim and occasionally unsettling, while Glimmer and the people he meets somehow keep the whole thing from ever feeling miserable.

Well Dweller 's demo is essentially its prologue, introducing the game's signature combat and traversal mechanics, and setting up the main narrative of Glimmer venturing out to find his family. Unfortunately, the demo ended just as that premise was set up, but it did so in a way that made me want more of this charming little game, with a cliffhanger that started out creepy and ended in chaos. Nevertheless, it did its job, as it sold me on what Well Dweller was trying to do and what it would potentially offer me down the road.

Traversal and Exploration Are the Heart of Well Dweller's Gameplay

It's possible that the full version of Well Dweller will have more of an emphasis on combat, but the bulk of what I played centered around traversal and exploration . On the traversal side, there's a simple jump action that can be slightly enhanced by holding the button down a bit longer. However, Glimmer can also slide—and it's quite satisfying to do—in order to fit through tighter passages and avoid damage. Rather than a standard dodge that so many metroidvanias seem to have, Well Dweller uses its slide ability for both exploration and combat, with slide actually making Glimmer invulnerable to damage while it's being executed. It's fun to use, for one thing, but it's also just satisfying hearing the soft sound it makes when the game's adorable little protagonist glides across the floor.

Well Dweller 's more distinctive traversal mechanics see Glimmer using bubbles to reach greater distances and a match—his primary weapon—to achieve greater heights. By attaching himself to a bubble, Glimmer can float in the direction of your choice, with the jump button then allowing him to leap out of the bubble in any other direction you choose. He can also throw his match like a slingshot to attach it to a surface, after which the match becomes a springboard he can use to jump a little higher. The bubbles and the slingshot-match combo were actually the two mechanics I used most during the demo to solve Well Dweller 's simple but fun traversal puzzles.

When I wasn't exploring or fighting off weird-looking monsters, I was charmed by the characters and the presentation, both visual and audible.

On the exploration side of things, however, there are collectibles to find and characters to meet . Apart from Glimmer's siblings and mother, whom I fell in love with almost instantly, I met a Looter NPC during Well Dweller 's demo that offered to sell me Trinkets in exchange for certain amounts of the game's currency—which you collect by defeating monsters. When I first stumbled upon him, there was only one item I could afford, a Flaming Vessel, which is essentially a molotov. But shortly after that, he appeared in my tent, the game's safe haven, and even expanded its interior and his inventory in the process. From there, I could return to him to purchase various Trinkets that, when equipped, offer unique gameplay bonuses.

There are plenty of collectibles to find , too, in the demo at least. But if this is a sign of what is to come in the full game, I'm looking forward to exploring every nook and cranny to find every single collectible item. There are simpler items, like pages to the fairy tale story Well Dweller 's world is based on, but there are other unique finds as well. During my demo playthrough, I stumbled on a couple of Trinket Slots, which allow me to equip more Trinkets, but Looter also sells plenty of those for a price. I also found a Spirit and brought it back to a little sanctuary where, afterward returning it, I was told there were 20 of them in total to collect and return. I'm not quite sure what their function is yet, or whether there will be more to find in other zones, but I always enjoy a good collectathon, regardless of what I'm searching for.

Well Dweller's Combat Still Does the Trick

But of course, if you're wondering whether Well Dweller 's combat is enough to justify its existence in the first place, you'll be happy to know that it is. I know I've basically painted this little indie gem out to be a lighter metroidvania, but I'll admit that I did die a few times, simply because I underestimated it . I'll also admit, with a little shame, that I didn't die during the demo's boss encounter—it was actually a few rank-and-file enemies that got me. Nevertheless, I found it immensely satisfying studying each enemy's combat patterns and then changing my own to counter them.

The only catch with Well Dweller , for anyone who prefers having a wide variety of combat skills in a metroidvania, is that its combat is fairly basic. Again, I'll throw a disclaimer in here that this is an observation based on the game's demo, and it's possible the full game could have a lot more going on when it comes to combat. However, even if it doesn't, combat is still somehow a lot of fun, because it mostly revolves around timing —learning an enemy's attack patterns and then carefully timing your own attacks.

During Well Dweller 's demo, I fought The Groundskeeper boss, who wasn't necessarily difficult, but still required me to pay close attention. Every enemy attack in the game is clearly indicated by the color pink, and as long as you're sliding when one of those pink symbols crosses in front of Glimmer, you'll avoid taking damage. The Groundskeeper's moveset was pretty simple, though, and once I learned it, I gave him a good several whacks with my match in between attacks.

But it's the enemy design, particularly the bosses, that really impressed me in Well Dweller . As I said earlier, they have this Tim Burton look about them, which is fitting, considering this is a fairy tale-like metroidvania and Burton has a knack for that space. With design like that, they don't really need to make me sweat bullets every time I encounter them. They're enough to look at and appreciate anyway.

If you're wondering whether Well Dweller 's combat is enough to justify its existence in the first place, you'll be happy to know that it is.

Despite my statement about the combat being simple, though, I did pick up that Flaming Vessel item I mentioned before, and it can be thrown out enemies—or thrown and then launched further by hitting it with the match—to inflict some ranged damage. That gives me at least a glimmer (pun intended) of hope that the full game will have more items that make combat even more exciting. It's also worth mentioning that there are some Trinkets that can passively deal damage to foes as well. I actually saw one in Looter's inventory that would automatically deal damage to enemies who damage Glimmer.

Well Dweller Is the Change of Pace I Didn't Know I Needed

Ultimately, Well Dweller 's demo gave me exactly what I didn't realize I wanted from a metroidvania right now. It has enough combat to keep me engaged and enough challenge to make me pay attention, but it never felt like it was constantly trying to punish me as so many other games in the genre do. Instead, I spent most of my time figuring out how to reach somewhere new, poking around for collectibles, meeting strange characters, and enjoying just how much personality Kyle Thompson has managed to squeeze into this weird little fairy tale. Between Glimmer sliding across the floor, launching himself from bubbles, springing off his own match, and taking on some genuinely creative-looking enemies, there was rarely a moment during the demo when I wasn't enjoying myself.

New Metroidvania Game on Steam Is Basically Dead Cells in Mexico
New Metroidvania Game on Steam Blends Silksong and Slime Rancher to Fix the Genre's Biggest Problem
New 2026 Metroidvania Game on Steam is Metroid Prime Meets Hollow Knight

More than anything, though, Well Dweller left me wanting to see what comes next. The demo only gives a small taste of its world, progression, combat, and story, and it ends right when things start getting particularly interesting, so I'm very curious to see how much all of those systems grow beyond the prologue. Thankfully, there isn't much longer to wait. Well Dweller launches September 22, 2026, for PC via Steam, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch, and Nintendo Switch 2 , and after what I played, it's absolutely one I'll be keeping an eye on when that day arrives.

Well Dweller
